clue.text: Cheats honest? Explain that!

parts.note: to con someone is to cheat them, so cheats gives cons
an honest account is a true one

explanation.surface: Someone challenged to justify how a fraudster could claim integrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheats honest?' reads as an outraged question, but it is just two pieces side by side; 'that!' is surface padding leading to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To construe a passage is to interpret it, which is a way of explaining its meaning.

clue.text: The wise man takes no rest

indicators.note: the letters of no rest take a new shape here, a loose signal to rearrange them

explanation.surface: A sage who never stops working.
explanation.walkthrough: Nestor is the old, wise counsellor of the Greeks in Homer's Iliad.
explanation.definitionFit: Nestor, the aged Greek king at Troy, is the classic figure of the wise elder counsellor.

clue.text: He had a model mother

parts.note: reads as praise of a good parent, but means a painter whose own mother sat as his model for a famous portrait

explanation.surface: Someone fondly recalling an exemplary parent.
explanation.walkthrough: The American painter James McNeill Whistler's best-known portrait is of his mother, usually called Whistler's Mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The artist painted his mother as the sitter for his most famous canvas, so she was literally his model.

clue.text: The grain being bad, had a meeting about it

indicators.note: the meeting word goes about the word for bad, holding it inside

parts.note: people who have had a meeting met
feeling bad means feeling ill

explanation.surface: Farmers gather to discuss a poor cereal harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: Millet is a small-seeded cereal crop, a kind of grain grown widely in Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Press left will get a scoop

parts.note: to press against something is to shove it

explanation.surface: An instruction that pushing a lever to the left will produce a ladleful.
explanation.definitionFit: A shovel is a broad-bladed tool used to scoop up earth or coal.

clue.text: Sailors may be seen around after midnight

indicators.note: the word seen goes around the morning abbreviation, holding it inside

parts.note: taken as written
AM marks the hours after midnight

explanation.surface: Sailors out late on shore leave can be spotted in the small hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Seamen are men who work on ships, another word for sailors.

clue.text: The endless stream causes a sensation

indicators.note: the word The loses its final letter, its end cut off

parts.note: a rill is a small stream or brook

explanation.surface: A never-ending flow of something produces a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as held had the next clue's words run on; the page prints only this. 'endless' takes the E off THE, leaving TH.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrill is a sudden feeling of excitement, a sensation of pleasure or fear.

clue.text: So slim, supple and lithe

indicators.note: something supple bends easily, so the letters of so slim are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A description of a slender, flexible figure.
explanation.walkthrough: All three words in 'slim, supple and lithe' look like synonyms; 'supple' is actually the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lissom means slender and graceful, moving with easy flexibility, just as lithe does.

clue.text: Cash remains — cash In contention repeatedly — to get torches

indicators.note: the three pieces before it go in the word for contention

parts.note: contention more than once gives fights, a plural
L, from the Latin libra, is the pound sign, so it stands for money
ash is what remains after burning
again L, the pound sign standing for money

explanation.surface: Money left over is fought over again and again until torches are bought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cash' reads as money in hand, but each 'cash' is the £ sign. 'in' puts LASHL inside the contention word, made plural by 'repeatedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Flashlights is the American word for electric torches, the hand-held battery lamps.

clue.text: Hound the fool getting into punt

indicators.note: the word for fool gets into the word for punt, sitting inside it

parts.note: a punt is a bet or gamble in British slang
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A dog follows a silly person climbing into a flat-bottomed boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' suggests the river boat, but here it is the British slang for a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: The basset is a short-legged breed of hunting dog with long ears.

clue.text: Inattentive, having no schedule

parts.note: a schedule is a list of things to do
the suffix less means having none, as in hopeless

explanation.surface: Someone unfocused because they have no plan for the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Listless means lacking energy or interest, so a listless pupil is inattentive.

clue.text: Tackle retreating soldiers for example

indicators.note: retreating soldiers go backwards, so the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a body of soldiers
EG abbreviates the Latin exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Troops falling back, given as an example of how to bring someone down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns the soldiers-plus-example run round, giving RAEG read backwards; British crosswords often use RA for gunners.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle as a noun is equipment, as in fishing tackle, which is also called gear.

clue.text: Variety of salt fish — see price

parts.note: the perch is a freshwater fish
lo is an old word meaning look or see
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: A fishmonger's list: salted fish, check the cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt fish' reads as one item, but 'salt' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A perchlorate is a chemical salt of perchloric acid, so it is one type of salt.

clue.text: On reflection they're helpful to motorists

definitions.text: On reflection they're helpful to motorists

parts.words: On reflection they're helpful to motorists
parts.note: on reflection seems to mean after thinking it over, but means by reflecting headlights: the road studs that guide drivers at night

explanation.surface: Musing on the things that make driving easier.
explanation.walkthrough: These are the reflective studs set into British road surfaces to mark lanes at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Small glass reflectors set in the road shine back car headlights, helping drivers see the lanes in the dark.

clue.text: Offering a suggestion to the personnel officer

parts.note: a tip is a helpful suggestion
the staff are the personnel of an organisation

explanation.surface: Giving advice to the head of human resources.
explanation.walkthrough: 'personnel officer' reads as one job title, but 'officer' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipstaff is a court official, a sheriff's or court officer who keeps order and makes arrests.

clue.text: Many a band shows great boldness

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, hence many
a ring is a band, as worn on a finger

explanation.surface: Lots of musical groups put on bold performances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests a music group, but it is a circular band.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring as a noun means audacity, a readiness to take bold risks.

clue.text: Hard as ever in the London area

indicators.note: the word ever goes in the two-letter London district

parts.note: SE is a London postal district, South East
taken as written

explanation.surface: Life in the capital is as tough as it has always been.
explanation.walkthrough: SE is the South East London postcode area.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe and hard both describe harsh, strict or difficult conditions, as in a hard winter.

clue.text: One can get intoxicated on non-alcoholic drink, and here's proof!

indicators.note: the word for intoxicated is placed on, after, the word for the drink

parts.note: water is the simplest drink with no alcohol
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A joke about getting drunk on soft drinks, offered as evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: Proof here is the suffix in waterproof, not evidence: a watertight seal is proof against water.
explanation.definitionFit: Something watertight is impervious to leaks, and an argument so described is beyond challenge.

clue.text: Simply lie — say fault developed

indicators.note: a fault that has developed has broken things, so the letters of lie and say are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to explain a breakdown with a plain fib.
explanation.definitionFit: Easily means without difficulty, which is what simply means in 'it simply worked'.

clue.text: Some eight went, yet there's still a fair number

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Even after eight have left, plenty remain.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included the OCR misreading 'stall'; the page prints 'still', and the definition is just 'a fair number'. Surface sense: twenty-eight less eight leaves twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty is a reasonably large count, the sort of quantity one would call a fair number.

clue.text: Look for sound support

indicators.note: the clue says the word for support is to be spoken, giving one that sounds the same

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar of a bridge or arch

explanation.surface: Searching for reliable backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning reliable, but signals the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: To peer is to look closely, narrowing the eyes to see.

clue.text: Set down letters in error — simplest mistake to make

indicators.note: a mistake here muddles the letters of simplest into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that bad spelling is the easiest error of all.
explanation.definitionFit: To have misspelt is to have written a word's characters wrongly.

clue.text: No way-out course!

explanation.definitionFit: Entree means a right of entry, the opposite of an exit, and is also a dish served as one stage of a meal.

clue.text: A vessel with room for food preparation

explanation.definitionFit: A galley is an oared ship, and also the kitchen on board a ship or aircraft.

clue.text: Check which is wrong in itself

indicators.note: things gone wrong are out of order, so the letters of itself are rearranged

explanation.surface: Investigating a thing that is inherently mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: To stifle something is to suppress or restrain it, which is to check it.
